# ContractPlane

> ContractPlane is the Agent Contract Plane: an early-stage proposal and reference kernel for transport-neutral, evidence-gated agent execution contracts.

ContractPlane is not Agent Client Protocol. It is also not the IBM/BeeAI-origin Agent Communication Protocol, whose documentation says it is now part of A2A under the Linux Foundation. Those protocols, along with MCP, may be used through future adapters.

## Current status

- Release: 0.1.0a1 alpha design/reference kernel.
- `contractplane.dev/v1alpha1` DomainPack is an alpha-candidate schema.
- RFD 0001 is Proposed and non-normative.
- The local state machine is the experimental `contractplane.dev/kernel-state/v0alpha1` profile.
- Implemented: DomainPack validation, deterministic ExecutionPlan compilation, local JSONL replay, manually registered units, output-schema checks, caller-supplied evidence receipts, and simple pre-dispatch authorization gating.
- Not implemented: Intent/Environment/Execution Contract resolution, selector or condition evaluation, binding invocation, runtime adapters, effective authority enforcement, independent Verdicts, steering invalidation, capability canary/promotion/rollback, or cross-runtime conformance.

Target architecture formula:

Intent + Domain Pack + Environment -> Execution Contract

Proposed core execution model:

Plan -> Unit -> Claim -> Evidence -> Verdict -> Transition

## Boundaries

- Agent runtimes such as Mastra, Codex, Claude, and LangGraph execute work.
- MCP, A2A, Agent Client Protocol, HTTP, and local CLI connect systems.
- The proposed ContractPlane architecture governs domain contracts, authority, evidence, steering, resumption, and capability lifecycle. The current v0.1 kernel implements only the subset listed above.
